title: [Optional] How to Deploy a Static Website onto the ICP Blockchain for Hosting
section: 39. Deploying to the ICP Live Blockchain
summary: Hosts a plain static website (the CSS-section demo site) on the Internet Computer: put the site in an assets folder, add a dfx.json describing one assets canister, flatten the file references, deploy with dfx deploy --network ic and open it at <canister-id>.ic0.app.

concepts.heading: Why host a static site on ICP
points: A small static site (HTML, CSS, a few images; only a couple of hundred KB) is an alternative to a hosting company or GitHub Pages.
Cost depends on the size of what is stored, so small sites cost very little cycles.
The lesson uses the course's earlier CSS website; the learner may use their own.

concepts.heading: Project layout and dfx.json
points: Create a project folder with a subfolder named assets that holds every site file (index.html, favicon, images, stylesheet). This mirrors the assets canister folder of the DBank project.
Next to (outside) the assets folder, create dfx.json, which tells dfx what canisters exist.
Inside it, define a canisters object with one canister named website. Its type is 'assets' and its source is an array (several folders are allowed) containing the path to the assets folder.
The canister name chosen here is the name used later in dfx canister --network ic id website.

concepts.heading: Flatten the file references
points: The deployment puts all asset files at the same level, collapsing subfolders such as css/ and images/ next to index.html and the favicon. Links with folder prefixes then break.
Edit index.html (search and replace) to drop the css/ prefix from the stylesheet link and the images/ prefix from the five image sources, leaving bare file names.

(Extra) The reference repo is already flat and uses ./styles.css, ./script.js and ./name.png image paths directly in the assets folder, matching this requirement. It also loads Google Fonts from a CDN, which still works because that is an external URL.
(Extra) Newer asset canisters keep folder structure, so this flattening step may not be needed with current dfx versions; test locally first.

concepts.heading: Deploy and visit
points: Open a terminal in the project folder and run dfx deploy --network ic. This creates the canister (spending wallet cycles) and uploads the assets.
Get the id with dfx canister --network ic id website, then open https://<id>.ic0.app. The site, including its favicon, loads from the blockchain and can be shared.
Keep the canister funded: when cycles run out the site can go offline, so top up the canister to keep it available.
Future course projects stay on local deployment to avoid cost.

task.name: Host a static website on the Internet Computer
task.starting_point: The CSS-section demo site (index.html, CSS folder, images, favicon), downloaded and unzipped, or your own small site.
task.goal: The site served live from an ICP canister at its ic0.app address.
steps: Put all site files in a folder called assets inside a project folder.
Create dfx.json beside assets with a canister called website of type assets with source ["assets"].
Flatten the references in index.html by removing the css/ and images/ prefixes (five image links).
Open a terminal in the project folder and run dfx deploy --network ic.
Run dfx canister --network ic id website to get the canister id.
Open https://<id>.ic0.app and share the link.
task.expected_result: The portfolio-style page loads with its styles, images and favicon from the canister URL.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 39 - Deploying to the ICP Live Blockchain/39.05 How to Deploy a Static Website onto the ICP Blockchain for Hosting/My Site/

pitfalls: Leaving folder prefixes in links after the flat upload gives missing CSS and images.
Running the terminal outside the project folder (it must contain dfx.json).
Letting the canister run out of cycles takes the site down.
Wrong canister name in the id command; it must match the name in dfx.json.

gaps_and_ideas: Optional lesson 'Hosting a static site': tasks on writing a dfx.json from a spec, rewriting asset paths to a flat layout, and spotting broken relative links.
Interactive demo idea: a file-tree toggle that flattens folders and highlights which src/href values break.
